busy: WRITE FROM THE WORN-OUT VIEWER'S SIDE

Before you write, picture one real person who is doing everything for everyone today and feels alone with it. Write so that person feels seen in the first two seconds, is never shamed, and leaves lighter.
depth: Mine Luke 10:38-42 for the details most people skip (who opened the house, where Mary sat, Martha's exact words, why Jesus says her name twice, 'one thing', 'shall not be taken away'). Build the film on the richest detail you find.
hook: Most viewers decide in 2 seconds. Write the strongest honest hook you can and make every line pull to the next. The payoff must be worth the wait.
plain: Write so a viewer with school English and no Bible knowledge understands every line on first hearing, and a lifelong Bible reader still learns something.
judge: Write the best film you can. Use your own judgment on everything.
